title: Bedřich Smetana's birth chart
metaDescription: Bedřich Smetana's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 11.9° Pisces. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Across the nine placements whose signs are settled, cardinal leads with five. The cardinal signs begin things; a chart weighted there treats every stall as a starting gun.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 11.9° Pisces. That falls in the second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by the Moon in the classical scheme — a water sign read through a mutable season.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 15.0° Aquarius; Venus stands at 4.4° Aquarius; Mars stands at 11.7° Libra. The tradition reads a mind at home in argument and pattern from Mercury, taste led by wit and proportion from Venus, drive that argues its way forward from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Jupiter and Pluto hold the closest angle here — a square, 0.0° wide. The old texts treat a square as the aspect you feel earliest and thank latest: obstruction first, competence afterwards. Behind it, Mars square Neptune at 2.5°, and the Sun sextile Neptune at 2.7° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, two sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Mars in Libra at 11.7° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Jupiter in Cancer at 1.1° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Tallied where the signs are certain — 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day — the chart gives air 3, earth 3, water 2, fire 1, and cardinal 5, fixed 3, mutable 1 across the modes. Air weights a chart toward language and pattern — the impulse to name a thing before deciding how to feel about it. Mars was retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Pisces into Aries during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.3° between one midnight and the next. Without a recorded hour there is no honest way to say which side it was on, so this reading does not say. The Moon sign is a real question here, not a rounding error, and it needs a birth time nobody has published.
